# Batch 10B — NexLearn V3 economic engine

**Status:** implemented on `feature/nexlearn-v3-integration` (local only; not pushed, merged or deployed).
**Engine:** `src/simulationV3/` (calibration `v3-econ-1.0`), production adapter `src/production/v3/adapter.ts`.
**Valuation:** NXLN-VAL-1.1 for V3 games. NXLN-VAL-1.0 is unchanged and still prices V2 games.
**Laboratory:** `scripts/lab/v3/`. Every number below comes from `docs/v3lab/tables.md`, regenerated by `V3LAB_WRITE=1 npx vitest run scripts/lab/v3/lab.test.ts`.

## 1. Architecture

| Concern | How it is handled |
|---|---|
| V2 stays frozen | `src/simulation/*` and `src/production/v2/adapter.ts` are byte-identical to `003f697`. Both `scripts/lab/batch9/lab.test.ts` and `scripts/lab/v3/lab.test.ts` assert this. |
| Separate V3 engine | `src/simulationV3/engineV3*.ts` is a fork of the 14 V2 engine modules. Exported names are unchanged, so the types are structurally identical. Every V3 change is guarded by a switch in `engineV3Config.ts` (`V3_ECONOMICS.mechanisms`). |
| Fork integrity | With every mechanism off, V3 path A reproduces V2 state-for-state for every Test Lab arc strategy (`src/production/v3/v3parity.test.ts`). It does the same for every laboratory strategy played through the production adapters (`scripts/lab/v3/lab.test.ts`). So every V2 → V3 difference traces to a named mechanism. |
| Dispatch | `src/production/v2/engine.ts` dispatches on the snapshot's `engineVersion`: `v2-econ-batch4-frozen` goes to the V2 adapter, `v3-econ-1.0` to the V3 adapter with the snapshot's `marketPath`. All UI, insight and persistence code calls the facade, not an adapter. |
| Existing sessions | V2 snapshots are unchanged and still validated by the strict V2 contract (which rejects `marketPath`). An existing session can never become V3: the engine comes from the session (see 10D migration), and `gameService` refuses a snapshot whose engine or path differs from its session. |
| Determinism | Pure functions only; no randomness. The laboratory checks that identical inputs give identical metrics, and that every V2 and V3 game replays exactly (`verifySnapshot`). |
| V3-only decisions in V2 games | The facade rejects `recessionStance` and `expansion` for V2 games, so the frozen adapter never silently drops them. |

## 2. Mechanisms implemented

All constants are in `src/simulationV3/engineV3Config.ts`.

| Id | Mechanism (one sentence a student can read) | Implementation | Constants |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E1** AI dominance | "AI-native revenue grows toward the level your AI adoption can support; it no longer adds new revenue every quarter forever." | `engineV3Revenue.ts` `aiRevenueTarget` and the convergence step. The target is the starting $4M plus revenue per adoption point above 10, gated by commercial readiness (40% → 100%), × demand × quality/execution × macro, capped at 90% of market capacity. Revenue closes `s` of the gap each quarter. Churn is implicit, and `target` is recorded in the diagnostic. | m = 0.30 per adoption point; s = 0.35 |
| **E2** Enterprise conversion | "Enterprise capability wins deals and they go live within two quarters; delivery teams still cost money." | Win rate per relative capability 0.08 → 0.2. Pipeline inflow amplitude 1.2 → 2.4. Recognition 25/50/25 → 50/50. Enterprise investment's recurring delivery commitment × 0.5 (4% → 2% of the investment per quarter for 6 quarters). | `V3_ECONOMICS.enterprise` |
| **E3** University conversion | "Institutions choose the stronger credential offer; partnerships go live over one to three quarters." | The institutional win rate adds 0.004 per point of relative Credential (bounds 15–55%). University inflow amplitude 0.8 → 4. Pipeline decided per quarter 20% → 30%. Recognition Q+1..Q+3 (30/40/30) instead of Q+2..Q+5. | `V3_ECONOMICS.university` |
| **E4** Organizational health | "Sustained change pressure wears culture down; a calm organization recovers, faster when People is funded; culture below its starting level strains execution, customer success and talent." | `applyOrganizationalHealth` (`engineV3Capabilities.ts`), applied after maturation and before the commercial step. Above a 0.6 load ratio, culture falls by 2 points per 0.1 (at most 4 per quarter). Below 0.5, it recovers 12% of the gap to 72 (× 0.5–1 with $0–10M People). Each culture point below 72 removes 0.06 Execution, 0.04 CS and 0.03 Talent per quarter (floor 20). Workforce-reduction aftershocks also hit Execution and CS (targeted −1.5/−1, deep −3/−2.5 for two quarters). The diagnostic `capability.organization` records every term. | `V3_ECONOMICS.organization` |
| **E9** Valuation NXLN-VAL-1.1 | "Investors also price the health of the organization." | New factor `organization` = mean of culture (40–90), talent (30–90) and execution (35–90) ramps, horizon "expectations". Weights: growth .25, profitability .20, readiness .20, retention .15, financial .12, organization .08. Selected by the game's engine (`valuationConfigFor`). VAL-1.0 weights and factors are unchanged (the existing test asserts them). | `VALUATION_CONFIG_V3` |

The 10C rules (E5 contract claim, E6 recession stance, E7 financing expansion) are also enforced by the V3 engine. They are reported in `BATCH10C_EXECUTIVE_DECISION_REPORT.md`, and the laboratory plays them in every V3 game.

**Teachability fix.** The V3 results text no longer claims "Culture paid for it" when culture did not move. It reports the actual overload loss, the recovery and the strain from `capability.organization` (V3 adapter `explainQuarter`). The V2 adapter text is frozen and unchanged.

## 3. The laboratory

`scripts/lab/v3/player.ts` plays a strategy through the **production adapters**, so every decision is validated exactly as in the classroom. The same player drives V2 and V3: the same Test Lab `DEFAULT_POLICY` for the contract, recession, crisis, Q8 and liquidity, and the same Batch 9 and Test Lab allocations. Where a V3 rule requires a decision, the player makes the one a sensible team would make:
- it holds the contract cost in reserve;
- it derives the stance from its recession actions;
- a hiring freeze moves People to reserve.

**Strategy set (17):**

| Category | Strategies |
|---|---|
| AI-heavy | AI-only, AI-led |
| Consumer-heavy | Consumer-only, Consumer-led |
| Enterprise-heavy | Enterprise-only, Enterprise-led, Enterprise + AI |
| University-heavy | University-only, University-led |
| People-heavy | People-only, Premium builder |
| Diversified | Diversified, Balanced |
| Cash preservation | Cash preservation |
| Adaptive | Evidence-responsive |
| Deliberately weak | Wrong-way, All reserve |

**Experiments (tables T1–T10):**
- V2 vs V3;
- mechanism attribution (each alone, all minus each);
- ±25% parameter sensitivity on 11 constants;
- four market variants;
- recession stances (8 strategies × 5 stances, plus a heavy-spending case);
- financing expansion X = 0/5/10/15;
- contract accept/decline with and without the budget claim;
- the marginal $5M by bucket.

**Invariants (asserted on every run):**
- the V2 freeze;
- accounting identities in every quarter of every game;
- exact replay of every snapshot;
- V3 with all mechanisms off equals V2;
- determinism;
- `withV3Economics` restores the configuration.

## 4. Findings (path A, the V2 market arc)

### AI dominance (E1)

| Measure | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|
| AI-only AI-native revenue at Q8 | $39M | $33M |
| AI-only price | $127.3 (rank 8) | $117.5 (rank 11) |
| AI-led price | $148.5 (rank 3) | $143.1 (rank 4) |
| Marginal $5M to AI/Product (from a balanced base), price | +$3.9 | −$0.1 |
| Marginal $5M to AI/Product, cumulative operating profit | +$15.4M | +$10.3M |

- In V2, the marginal $5M to AI was the only clearly positive bucket. In V3 it is still the best bucket for operating profit (T10).
- With AI-native demand held neutral (T6, "no-AI-disruption"), AI-only falls to rank 15 of 17. Its value is now market-dependent.
- The top of the ranking is still AI-combined strategies: Premium builder, Adaptive, Enterprise + AI. That fits an AI-transformation arc, but in path A AI remains the most valuable single capability.

### Enterprise conversion (E2)

| Measure | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise-only Enterprise revenue | $52M | $65M (+63% vs the $40M start) |
| Enterprise-led Enterprise revenue | $50M | $62M |
| Enterprise-only price | $74.7 (rank 15) | $104.1 (rank 14) |
| Enterprise-led price | $81.8 (rank 14) | $112.6 (rank 12) |

- Enterprise-led is now a credible, slower-payback strategy. It is still below the AI combinations in path A, because path A is an AI-first market.
- Its competitive test is path B (10D).
- With the claim, the contract is worth +$14.8 for Enterprise-led and +$11.8 for Enterprise-only, against −$6.8 for Consumer-led (T9).

### University conversion (E3)

| Measure | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|
| University-led University revenue at Q8 | $15M | $19.6M (+23%) |
| University-only University revenue at Q8 | $15M | $20.4M (+27%) |
| University-led price | $110.9 (rank 11) | $127.0 (rank 7) |
| University-only price | $111.1 | $121.6 |

- Growth is visible from Q5 ($17.1M).
- The largest quarter-over-quarter step is +$2.1M, under the +$4M "instant revenue" limit.
- The Q7 crisis briefly dips University revenue for University-led strategies.
- Raising the University win rate further has almost no effect: ±25% moves the price by under $1 (T5). The binding factor is the pipeline and the time left in eight quarters, which is the credible constraint for institutional sales.

### Organizational health and layoffs (E4, E9)

Q8 effect of a deep workforce reduction versus "protect" (T7):

| Measure | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|
| Price | −$3.6 to +$16.0; positive for 7 of 8 strategies | −$19.3 to +$3.7; negative for 6 of 8 |
| Cumulative operating profit | +$35–45M | +$29–43M |
| CFO score | higher | still higher |
| Culture | −20 | −13 to −26 |

- The saving is real but no longer free.
- **Not universally wrong:** for University-led (+$3.7) and Consumer-led (+$0.3), a deep cut still raises the price slightly, and every cut raises operating profit and the CFO score.
- A targeted cut sits in between: −$8.5 to +$3.2.
- Overload now matters for broad, high-load plans:
  - Diversified (three $10M initiatives; peak load ratio 0.79) ends with culture 55, and its price falls from $143.8 to $136.8.
  - Wrong-way ends with culture 61.
  - Focused plans and People-funded plans keep culture near 72.

### Consumer relevance

- Consumer strategies are unchanged in path A: Consumer-led $116.2 → $118.3; Consumer-only $109.9 → $107.3. In an AI-disruption arc, competitors' consumer AI erodes the base.
- In the "no-AI-disruption" variant they gain ranks (Consumer-led 10 → 9, Consumer-only 13 → 12) and AI-only loses four.
- Consumer's real test is path C (Economic Pressure), authored in 10D. 10B adds no consumer-specific mechanism: the evidence did not support one, and the starting mix stays unchanged as approved.

### Valuation review (NXLN-VAL-1.1)

- The organization factor costs strategies that run the organization down: Diversified −$6.9; deep cuts as above.
- It does not change healthy strategies by more than about $2 (T4 "only organizationalHealth" column).
- Price-ranking correlation V2 → V3 is 0.95. The model is recognisably the same; the mechanism changes move specific strategies, not the whole board.

### Dominance

- **No strategy leads on every measure in V3.**

  | Measure | Leader |
  |---|---|
  | Price | Premium builder ($152.3) |
  | Terminal score | Adaptive (80.1) |
  | Cumulative operating profit | Diversified ($275M) |
  | Executive team score | Adaptive (76.7) |

- Across the four market variants:
  - the top strategy is always Premium builder or Adaptive;
  - Spearman correlation against path A is 0.96–1.00, so the variants are not different enough to change the ranking (T6).
- **The ranking does not change much between market variants of path A.** That is expected: they edit demand, not the authored signals. Path-level differences are the job of 10D (paths B and C) and are validated in 10F (H1, H2, H9, H10).

### Sensitivity

- ±25% on any of the 11 calibrated constants keeps the price ranking (Spearman ≥ 0.98).
- The top strategy stays Premium builder or Adaptive.
- The largest single move is −$10.9 for AI-only when m is cut by 25% (T5).
- **The conclusions do not depend on a knife-edge calibration.**

## 5. Calibration decisions

| Constant | Tested | Chosen | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI revenue per adoption point (m) | 0.25 / 0.30 / 0.42 | **0.30** | 0.42 overshot V2 (AI-only $43M). 0.25 cut AI-led by $14 and moved AI-led to rank 7. 0.30 keeps AI-led top-4 in path A with AI-only mid-table. |
| AI convergence speed (s) | 0.30 / 0.35 | **0.35** | Insensitive (±$4). |
| University inflow amplitude and resolution | 3 & 0.2 / 4 & 0.3 / 5 & 0.3 | **4 & 0.3** | Reaches about $20M (+23–27%) by Q8 without instant revenue; 5 adds only about $1M. |
| Overload threshold / culture per 0.1 / cap | 0.9 / 1.5; 0.65; 0.6 / 2; 0.55 / 2 | **0.6 / 2 / 4 per quarter** | At 0.9 the mechanism never fired: the peak load of the tested strategies is 0.26–0.79. 0.55 eroded culture for adaptive play too. Without a per-quarter cap, a deep cut on a high-load plan drove culture to 16. |
| Recovery below / share | 0.7 / 0.5 | **0.5 / 12%** | Recovery must not overlap the overload band. |

## 6. Limitations

- Market sensitivity in 10B uses variants of path A. The authored paths B and C, and the hypotheses that need them (H1, H2, H9, H10), are tested in 10F.
- The game has eight quarters. The design's Q12 checks for layoffs (H4) cannot be run without exceeding the scope, so long-run costs are judged at Q8 (price, culture, terminal and People scores).
- The laboratory plays policies, not people. Classroom behaviour (for example, how often teams use expansion) is not validated.
- The stance and the contract claim are rules: they change which plans are allowed, not the formulas. Their economic effect shows through the plans teams choose (T7, T9).
